# Synthetic Development Cohort — `synthetic_cohort.csv`

**This is not real patient data.** It is generated by
`backend/scripts/generate_synthetic.py` so that the full Digital Twin pipeline
could be built, trained and tested while institutional approval for clinical data
is still in progress. No number in this file came from a patient.

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | 4,800 (one row per patient-visit) |
| Patients | 600 |
| Visits per patient | 8, at ~6-month intervals |
| Follow-up span | 3.5 years per patient (2021-01 → 2025-07) |
| Columns | 18 |

---

## Column dictionary

| Column | Type | Unit | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patient_key` | string | — | De-identified study key, stable across visits |
| `visit_date` | date | YYYY-MM-DD | |
| `age` | float | years | Age at this visit |
| `sex` | string | — | male / female |
| `parental_myopia` | int | count | 0, 1 or 2 short-sighted parents |
| `spherical_equivalent` | float | dioptres (D) | Negative = short-sighted. **Primary target** |
| `axial_length` | float | mm | Length of the eye. **Primary target** |
| `visual_acuity` | float | logMAR | 0.00 ≈ 6/6 vision |
| `corneal_curvature` | float | mm | Mean keratometry radius |
| `treatment` | string | — | none / single_vision / atropine / ortho_k / dims |
| `screen_time_hours` | float | h/day | Behaviour layer |
| `near_work_min` | float | min/day | Behaviour layer |
| `outdoor_min` | float | min/day | Behaviour layer |
| `sleep_hours` | float | h/night | Behaviour layer |
| `viewing_distance_cm` | float | cm | Ergonomic layer |
| `posture_score` | float | 0–1 | 1 = upright and well supported |
| `continuous_session_min` | float | min | Time before a break |
| `source` | string | — | Always `synthetic` |

---

## Missing values are deliberate

Behaviour and ergonomic fields are **blanked for a random subset of visits**, to
mirror the fact that real clinics do not record them consistently:

| Layer | Missing |
|---|---|
| Ergonomics (`viewing_distance_cm`, `posture_score`, `continuous_session_min`) | 22.1 % |
| Behaviour (`screen_time_hours`, `near_work_min`, `outdoor_min`, `sleep_hours`) | 12.1 % |
| Clinical (`spherical_equivalent`, `axial_length`) | 0 % |

Missing stays missing — the models (HistGradientBoosting) accept NaN natively,
so no value is ever imputed with a guess.

---

## How the values were generated

Each patient is given a starting refraction, biometry and a set of behavioural
tendencies. Progression to the next visit is drawn from a hand-written annual
rate:

```
annual_SE_change = 0.05
                 + 0.42·exp(−0.16·(age−6))      # younger eyes progress faster
                 + 0.10·(parental myopia count) # heredity
                 − 0.0018·(outdoor_min − 70)    # outdoor time protective
                 + 0.0005·(near_work_min − 200)
                 + 0.018·(screen_time − 4)
                 − 0.010·(viewing_distance − 31)
                 + 0.0010·(session_length − 45)
                 − 0.08·(posture − 0.65)
                 − 0.03·(current SE)
                 × treatment effect             # atropine 0.55, ortho-k 0.60, DIMS 0.62
                 + N(0, 0.12)                   # biological noise
```

Axial length is coupled to refractive change (≈0.38 mm per dioptre) plus a
baseline growth term.

**The directions** (younger age, parental myopia, more near work and less
outdoor time associate with faster progression) follow what is reported in the
myopia literature. **The magnitudes are illustrative.**

---

## Calibration check

The generator was tuned so the cohort sits in a clinically plausible range
rather than an implausible one:

| Statistic | This cohort | Typical school-age range |
|---|---|---|
| Mean annual SE change | −0.40 D/year | ≈ −0.4 to −0.6 D/year |
| Final SE (median) | −2.45 D | — |
| Final SE (10th–90th pct) | −4.43 to −0.60 D | — |
| Final axial length (median) | 24.50 mm | ≈ 22–26 mm |

---

## Important limitation to state in any report

Because the data comes from a deterministic equation, it is **more learnable
than real data**. Models reach R² ≈ 0.99 on it, and a linear (Ridge) model
currently achieves the lowest error — precisely because the generator is close
to linear in its inputs. These figures demonstrate that the pipeline works end to
end; **they are not clinical performance results** and will be substantially
lower on real, noisier cohorts.

---

## Where this file appears in the running application

Every patient in the Iiris database is loaded from this CSV — nothing in the app
is hand-written. A reviewer can pick any number on screen and find it here.

| In the app | Cohort key(s) | Visits |
|---|---|---|
| Research cohort (25 patients) | `SYN00000` … `SYN00024` | 200 |
| Sign-in account `demo@iiris.health` ("Aarav Nair") | `SYN00532` | 8 |
| Sign-in account `clear@iiris.health` ("Rohan Iyer") | `SYN00328` | 8 |

Verified: 27 patients, 216 visits, checked row by row against this file — zero
mismatches, and no patient in the database that is absent from it.

The two sign-in accounts were chosen from the **well-covered** part of the
distribution (final SE about −2.5 to −3.0 D). Below roughly −4 D the cohort thins
out and the independently fitted quantile models begin to disagree with the
median model, which pushes the point estimate toward the edge of its own
interval (measured: well centred for 98% of rows between −1 and −3 D, off-centre
for 55% of rows below −4 D). A demonstration should show a representative
patient rather than a tail case; the API flags the disagreement per record when
it occurs.

```bash
# reproduce the check
cd backend && python scripts/seed_users.py --reset
```

---

## Reproducing this file

```bash
cd backend
python scripts/generate_synthetic.py          # default: 600 patients, seed 20260908
```

The generator is deterministic given its seed, so the same file can be
regenerated exactly.

## Replacing it with real data

The column contract is identical. Required columns are `patient_key`,
`visit_date`, `spherical_equivalent` and `axial_length`; everything else is
optional and may be omitted entirely. See `docs/DATA_ONBOARDING.md`.
